text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The dollar-leu rate dropped by some 1,000 lei for a dollar on the black market to 4,500 lei for a dollar.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Refineries will be running out of crude stocks in the next four days, the Romanian Oil Company (CRP) said.
ADEVARUL
- Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea is to meet IMF negotiators to discuss priorities in his government programme.
- The CRP received a $30 million last-minute credit to buy 200,000 tonnes of crude to cover a steep shortage.
- Romania will become in 1998 East Europe's third largest recipient for foreign investments after Russia and Poland, National Bank (BNR) deputy-governor Vlad Soare says in interview.
- Vacaroiu said he had never understood the IMF, saying the Fund should have helped Romania more by giving it credits faster to allow the country to reach macro-economic targets.
- The Rovinari thermal power plant registered a 40 billion lei loss in the first 10 months of 1996.
LIBERTATEA
- The Navrom shipping company is expected to call a tender to sell 26 ships which are older than the 20-year limit.
- BNR governor Mugur Isarescu pleads for the bank's autonomy.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Romania's refineries are confronted with a crude shortage, while oil tankers are blocked in the Black Sea port of Constanta due to lack of finance to pay for imports.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- State-owned Bancorex bank will finance energy imports.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- President-elect Emil Constantinescu said his Democratic Convention (CDR) rejected any attempt to invalidate outgoing President Ion Iliescu's mandate as a senator, elected on the the list of the leftist Party of Social Democracy (PDSR).
- The Constitutional Court validated Constantinescu's election as president in the November 17 run-off.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- State television must not be subordonated to the government, Vartan Arachelian, TV producer, says in an interview.

- Ciorbea said the accord concluded by the CDR and former Prime Minister Petre Roman's Social Democratic Union (USD) ahead of the presidenial run-off will be respected in the new coalition government and its programme.
ADEVARUL

- Following the first day of negotiations for the new coalition government, the National Peasant Party (PNT-CD), the main party in the CDR, gets 10 ministries, the National Liberal Party (PNL) five, the USD seven and the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) one.
- The newspaper publishes the message adressed by President Bill Clinton to Romania's outgoing President Ion Iliescu.
- Oliviu Gherman resigned from his position as president of the PDSR, leaving his place for Ion Iliescu who, he said, is the soul and father of the party.
- The newspaper publishes the list of deputies and senators who are in the new parliament which starts its session today.
- The newspaper publishes an interview with the parents of Victor Ciorbea, who live in a village in the western Apuseni mountains and have not seen their son as their television set is broken.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Roman's USD will not oppose Iliescu's validation as senator.

- France's former Defence Minister Charles Hernu never spied for Romania, said Ion Pacepa, former head of the Securitate secret police under dictator Nicolae Ceausescu until he defected to the United States in 1977.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Young peopole must enter politics, says Radu Ghidau, 23, Romania's youngest deputy elected in the general elections earlier this month.
JURNALUL NATIONAL

- Bogdan Hossu, head of the Alfa trade union confederation says in an interview he hopes that Ciorbea will not forget that he was a union leader himself. ($=3,509 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
